skill.name: generating-rbs
skill.description: Generates RBS type signatures for Ruby source files by analyzing classes, modules, methods, constants, and type relationships.
skill.summary: Create pure RBS signatures for Ruby projects from existing source code.
skill.author: DmitryPogrebnoy

security_audit.summary: The reported static findings are false positives from bundled RBS reference signatures, Ruby standard library API declarations, Markdown formatting, and vendored Zeitwerk examples. No evidence of prompt injection, credential theft, malicious network use, or hidden command execution was found in the reviewed context. Static review was capped at 400/1166 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 766 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Large bundled reference corpus triggers many static false positives.
remediation.suggestion: Document that reference files are examples only, or reduce bundled examples to the minimum needed for RBS generation guidance.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs users to run validation commands such as rbs validate and steep check.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command execution limited to explicit validation steps and continue to avoid running application Ruby code.

- [ ] Step 3: Eliminate `untyped` types in generated signatures
- You MUST not use `untyped`. Infer the proper type instead.
- You MUST prepend any command with `bundle exec` if the project has Gemfile.
- Create necessary `.rbs` files for the target Ruby file.
- Place generated RBS files in `sig/` directory mirroring Ruby source structure.
- Pay extra attention to `Data` and `Struct` types. See [data_and_struct.md](reference/data_and_stru
- Go through all generated signatures and replace `untyped` with the proper type.
- If you cannot infer the proper type, leave it as `untyped`.
- Try to get rid of any unnecessary `untyped` types.
- Run `rbs validate` to verify that existing and new `.rbs` files are internally consistent. It will
- Fix any errors reported by `rbs validate` and repeat the process until there are no errors.
Perform this step ONLY if the project Gemfile includes `steep` gem AND the project has Steepfile.
- Run `steep check` to verify that generated RBS signatures are type safe.
- Fix any errors reported by `steep check` and repeat the process until there are no errors.
- Roll back to step 4 if you fixed any errors reported by `steep check`.

content.value_statement: Ruby projects often lack complete RBS signatures, which limits static type checking. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through generating and validating pure RBS files from Ruby source.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes Ruby classes, modules, methods, constants, inheritance, and visibility.
Creates new pure RBS signature files under a mirrored sig directory structure.
Uses bundled RBS syntax and Ruby core or standard library examples as references.
Reduces avoidable untyped annotations by inferring types from source and tests.
Validates generated signatures with rbs validate when command execution is approved.
Runs steep check only when the project includes Steep configuration.
limitations: Does not update existing RBS signatures or handle RBS-inline annotations.
May leave untyped when source and tests do not provide enough type evidence.
Requires manual review for metaprogramming-heavy Ruby code.
Validation commands depend on local Ruby tools and project configuration.

use_cases.title: Add types to a Ruby library
use_cases.description: Generate initial RBS files for library classes before introducing static type checks.

use_cases.title: Prepare an application for Steep
use_cases.description: Create signatures that can be validated before adding type checking to a Ruby application.

use_cases.title: Document public Ruby interfaces
use_cases.description: Produce readable RBS signatures that describe methods, constants, and object shapes.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a first RBS file
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one Ruby source file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate pure RBS signatures for this Ruby file and place them in the matching sig path. Avoid untyped unless no type can be inferred.

prompt_templates.title: Type a small module
prompt_templates.scenario: Several related files need consistent signatures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these Ruby files as one module and generate coherent RBS signatures for their public and private APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Refine generated signatures
prompt_templates.scenario: A draft signature exists but needs stronger types.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these generated RBS signatures against the Ruby source and tests. Replace avoidable untyped entries with inferred concrete types.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and repair RBS
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with local validation tools.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate RBS signatures, run rbs validate, fix all reported issues, and run steep check only if this project has Steep configured.

output_examples.input: A Ruby service class with initializer arguments, public methods, and private helper methods.
output_examples.output: A matching RBS signature summary with constructor types, method return types, visibility sections, and notes about inferred assumptions.

output_examples.input: A Ruby Struct or Data object with typed attributes and factory methods.
output_examples.output: A concise RBS description that captures attribute readers, initialization shape, and value object behavior.

output_examples.input: A Ruby module that mixes in dependencies and defines constants.
output_examples.output: A signature plan covering module methods, included modules, constants, and validation steps.

best_practices: Provide source files, tests, and expected public API boundaries together.
Review generated signatures before relying on type checker results.
Run validation after each meaningful signature change.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to execute application Ruby code to infer behavior.
Do not accept broad untyped signatures when source evidence supports stronger types.
Do not use this skill for RBS-inline migration or existing signature maintenance.

faq.question: Does this skill execute my Ruby application?
faq.answer: No. The instructions explicitly say not to run project Ruby code while generating signatures.

faq.question: Where are generated signatures placed?
faq.answer: The skill places new RBS files in the sig directory, mirroring the Ruby source structure.

faq.question: Can it update existing RBS files?
faq.answer: No. It is designed to generate pure RBS signatures from scratch.

faq.question: Does it support RBS-inline?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that it does not handle RBS-inline signatures.

faq.question: Will it always avoid untyped?
faq.answer: It tries to infer concrete types, but may use untyped as a last resort when evidence is insufficient.

faq.question: When does it run steep check?
faq.answer: It runs steep check only when the project has both the Steep gem and a Steepfile.
